blockers.symptom: pnpm typecheck exited 2 with two findings: server/services/repository.ts(51,17) rejected RepositoryPolicy<RepositoryRecord> against RepositoryPolicy<T> at .withPolicy(policy), and server/services/tokens.ts(3-10) could not resolve ./assistant.js, ./dashboard.js, ./devices.js, ./external.js, ./inspections.js, ./knowledge.js, ./manuals.js and ./work-orders.js.
blockers.rootCause: scopedRepository declared its policy parameter as the default RepositoryPolicy (RepositoryRecord) but connection.repository<T>() expects RepositoryPolicy<T>, so the bridge between the authorization policy type and the concrete row type was missing. Separately, the implementation run declared one DI token per business service but never wrote the service modules those type-only imports named, and nothing imported the token module, so the references could never resolve.
blockers.resolution: Kept scopedRepository's public parameter as the general RepositoryPolicy and cast at the withPolicy call (policy as RepositoryPolicy<T>) so the typing seam the module documents stays in one place; the return value was already cast to ScopedRepository<T>. Removed the unreferenced server/services/tokens.ts, which had no importers and named modules that do not exist; reintroduce tokens together with their service contracts when those services are implemented. Verified with `pnpm typecheck` (exit 0), `prettier --check server/services/repository.ts` and `eslint server/services/repository.ts`.

blockers.title: After-sales business application is still largely unimplemented
blockers.symptom: Working tree only adds database/main/migrations/202610010001_create_service_collections.ts, server/business/{resources,register,record-access,work-order-state}.ts and a few server/services helpers. There are no HTTP routes (server/routes/index.ts is empty), no service providers (server/providers/index.ts is empty), no work-order/device/inspection/knowledge/manual/external/dashboard/assistant services, no workflow or scheduler definitions, no business pages or client routes, no seeds, and no business tests.
blockers.rootCause: The implementation run ended after producing schema, authorization resources and helper seams, without the service, route, provider, scheduling, client and seed layers the requirements need. The verification pipeline stopped at the first gate (typecheck), so those gaps were never exercised.
blockers.resolution: Superseded by repair 2, which built the missing layers: server/services/{access,service-desk,service-desk-impl}.ts, server/routes/{service,resources}.ts, server/providers/{service-desk,ai-resources,scheduled-tasks}.ts, server/business/{permission-config,provision,scheduled-tasks}.ts, server/locales, the workflow package under server/workflows/work-order-auto-accept, the schema migration, client pages under client/pages/service plus routes/navigation/i18n, and the AI employee/tool resources under server/ai. The previous open record is retained for history.

blockers.title: Application was the blank default template: no business nav, pages or APIs
blockers.symptom: QA observed the homepage as the NocoBase placeholder with only Home in the main nav, /main/customers redirected to /main, GET /main/api/customers:list returned the SPA HTML, no test accounts beyond Super Admin, no workflow definitions/runs, no scheduled tasks, empty permission resources and no business pages.
blockers.rootCause: The working tree carried only the template starting point: no business collections were seeded, no service providers or routes were registered, no client routes or pages existed, and no demo accounts/permission sets were provisioned. The template already registered every plugin in client/plugins.ts and server/plugins.ts, so the plugin capabilities were present but nothing application-owned used them.
blockers.resolution: Implemented the application-owned slice end to end: added the service collections migration, the service-desk service with role/record scoping, HTTP routes under /api/service plus resource-style aliases, providers that register the service and provision demo permission sets/accounts/records at start(), client business pages (dashboard, customers, customer detail, devices, work orders, work-order detail, inspections, knowledge, manuals, assistant) declared in client/routes.ts with navigation and zh/en locale entries, server locales for scheduled/notification text, the auto-accept workflow package, scheduler targets, attachments through the file plugin, external API-key integration, and the AI employee/tool resources. Verified: GET /api/customers:list returns JSON for a signed-in supervisor, demo accounts sign in, permission sets carry page/action grants, scheduler lists two active schedules, accepts produce workflow runs, and the in-app inbox contains persisted messages.

blockers.title: GET /api/customers:list returned the SPA shell instead of JSON; wildcard middleware answered unregistered API paths
blockers.symptom: The QA feedback showed GET /main/api/customers:list returned doctype HTML, and the app-server test 'starts a fresh Default without example tables or APIs' failed because unregistered paths such as /api/articles were intercepted with 401 instead of falling through to the SPA.
blockers.rootCause: server/routes/resources.ts mounted its alias router at /api and installed two catch-all routes.use('*', ...) middlewares (authentication plus service-access resolution) before registering the aliases. The wildcard matched every API path, so both unregistered paths and the aliases were captured by the middleware chain, and the QA path name /api/customers:list either matched nothing usable or was shadowed. This is the same router.use('*') cross-contribution leak AGENTS.md warns against.
blockers.resolution: Removed the catch-all middlewares and attached the resolved `authenticated` handler and a `withServiceAccess` middleware to each registered alias route individually (list/get/create/update/destroy). Unregistered API paths now fall through to the SPA shell again, while the aliases are authenticated and scope the caller to the approved service. Verified: anonymous /api/articles returns 200 text/html, anonymous /api/customers:list returns 401, and a signed-in supervisor gets JSON.

blockers.title: Source-managed auto-accept workflow never executed (trigger reported skipped/not-found)
blockers.symptom: After registering the workflow package, accepting a work order returned 200 but /api/workflows showed no current revision and /api/workflow-runs stayed empty; automation.trigger returned {status:'skipped', reason:'not-found'}.
blockers.rootCause: A workflow compiled from a source package is materialized disabled and is not discovered until something asks for it, so the workflow service looked up a revision whose `current` pointer was null and skipped the trigger. Nothing in the application activated its own revision.
blockers.resolution: Added a duck-typed AutoAcceptWorkflowRuntime contract in server/services/automation.ts and materializeAutoAcceptWorkflow(), which discovers the shipped artifact and calls the workflow loader's ensureArtifactMaterialized(digest) instead of editing the materialized workflow tables. Wired it in ServiceDeskProvider.start() through a guarded resolveWorkflowRuntime() and left the source definition enabled:false, letting the application activate its own revision at startup. Verified: the log reports 'auto-accept workflow activated (1)', /api/workflows shows current:true, and an accept produces workflow-runs with status 1.

blockers.title: Client route page authz ids did not match the seeded service-* permission grants
blockers.symptom: The business routes declared page authz ids dashboard/customers/devices/workOrders/inspections/knowledge/manuals while server/business/permission-config.ts seeded the corresponding service-dashboard/service-customers/... grants. A grant is keyed by the page id, so no non-admin user would have matched any business page and the pages would be hidden from every demo role.
blockers.rootCause: The page id is the identity stored in page grants; the client routes and the provisioning constants were written independently and drifted. The mismatch is silent at build time and only denies access at runtime.
blockers.resolution: Unified the ids on service-* (matching both the route name and the seeded grants), added a service-assistant page id, and added the assistant route so the assistant participates in the same grant model. Verified by the client-routes test (which pins the authorized page list) and by confirming the provisioned sets contain service-work-orders and service-assistant grants.

blockers.title: No AI service-assistant surface and no page-context grounding
blockers.symptom: QA found no service assistant or work-order page, so it could not verify that suggestions become a handling-note draft, that cancel does not write, that confirmation saves, or that the app never auto-closes.
blockers.rootCause: The AI Employee plugin ships no application chat UI and the application had no employee, tool or page context of its own.
blockers.resolution: Installed the plugin's own shipped Registry chat UI into client/extensions/nocobase-ai, defined an app-owned service-assistant AI employee plus a read-only work-order context tool in server/ai, and mounted the UI through client/components/service-assistant.tsx. Added a dedicated /assistant page and a floating panel on the work-order detail page, wrapped in a single ServiceAssistantBoundary so page-context registrations and the chat share one registry. The assistant writes only into a visible handling-note draft (form id work-order-handling-note); the transition dialog copies the draft into its note and the engineer confirms and saves explicitly, so nothing is persisted before confirmation and the workflow is never auto-closed. A useAssistantReady() gate shows the real readiness state (loading, no employees, no model) instead of a broken composer. Verified: /api/ai/aiEmployees:listByUser returns atlas and service-assistant, listLLMServices is [] so the gate shows the no-model message, and the page/test typechecks load the component.

blockers.title: Observer could reach the work-order state machine before the role check
blockers.symptom: An observer POSTing a transition to an order in the wrong state received 409 STATE_CONFLICT with the order code, proving the request passed authorization and reached the domain state machine.
blockers.rootCause: transitionWorkOrder called findWorkOrder and checked the status transition before calling assertTransitionAllowed, so a read-only role learned state and could in principle act whenever the status happened to be valid.
blockers.resolution: Moved assertTransitionAllowed ahead of the status-conflict check so authorization is decided before the persisted state is revealed or acted on. Verified with a dev run: the observer now receives 403 FORBIDDEN for both transition and customer creation, while the supervisor still accepts successfully.

blockers.title: app-server logic tests failed: providers assumed optional plugins, and the alias wildcard leaked
blockers.symptom: tests/logic/app-server.test.ts failed twice: ServiceDeskProvider.boot() threw 'Service "@nocobase/app/authorization" is not registered' in a minimal app with no authorization plugin, and the fresh-Default test got 401 for unregistered GET paths.
blockers.rootCause: The provider boot path resolved authorizationToken unconditionally, unlike the sibling providers that guard optional tokens, and the resource alias router's catch-all use('*') middleware intercepted every API path.
blockers.resolution: Guarded ServiceDeskProvider.boot() with container.has(authorizationToken) (matching AIResourcesProvider and ScheduledTasksProvider) and made authorization optional for a minimal host, and removed the alias catch-all as described above. The provider's register() already binds a lazy singleton, so nothing resolves authorization until a caller needs the service. Verified: vitest run tests/logic passes 25 files / 176 tests and the full suite passes 41 files / 307 tests.

blockers.title: Real AI Q&A/retrieval cannot run in this environment
blockers.symptom: The AI Knowledge Base create action fails with 'vectorDatabaseKey is required for LOCAL knowledge bases', no vector database provider other than PGVector is registered, and ai:listLLMServices returns []. There is therefore no embedding service or vector store to process the two Markdown manuals.
blockers.rootCause: The environment provides zero LLM services and no vector database connection, which are prerequisites for knowledge-base vectorization and retrieval. Both are deployment/credential concerns outside the application source.
blockers.resolution: Kept the AI Knowledge Base plugin registered and its page reachable (the QA-observed 404 is gone; the management API returns 200), left the assistant's real readiness state visible, and kept manual work-order handling fully usable. The two manuals are now genuinely uploaded into an app-owned knowledge base and carry their real document link and processing state (see the repair-4 manuals entry); with no embedding service or vector store the upload reports its real 'Vector database ... not found' error rather than a fabricated Ready. Per the task, real Q&A and retrieval are still recorded as blocked/not_run rather than faked with fixed answers, because they require an enabled LLM/embedding service and a vector database.

blockers.title: Duplicate device code returned 500 and a work order accepted a customer/device mismatch
blockers.symptom: POST /api/service/devices with an existing code surfaced as 500 Internal Server Error; POST /api/service/work-orders with a customer and a device owned by another customer returned 201 and created the order.
blockers.rootCause: createDevice/updateDevice relied on the database unique constraint instead of pre-checking the code, so the driver error escaped as 500; createWorkOrder never verified that the selected device belongs to the selected customer or is enabled, so the two lookups were independent.
blockers.resolution: Added assertDeviceCodeAvailable(code, exceptId?) which trims and pre-checks the code across other rows and raises 409 CONFLICT; createWorkOrder now resolves the customer, requires the device to exist (404), to belong to the customer (400), and to be enabled (409). Verified with npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json and the service/permission tests.

blockers.title: Production workflow auto-accept could not resolve @nocobase/db and left acceptance_note null
blockers.symptom: Accepting a work order did not write acceptance_note, and the workflow node run logged "Cannot find package '@nocobase/db'".
blockers.rootCause: The workflow artifact store used the default local disk rooted under storage, so in a deployment the materialized artifact modules resolved their bare imports relative to a directory outside the bundled node_modules tree.
blockers.resolution: Registered a `workflows` file-system drive disk at paths.root('workflow-artifacts') (inside the code root, next to node_modules in every deployment), set workflow.artifactDisk to `workflows` with sourceRoot/distRoot = paths.server('workflows') and a deploymentRootDir. Verified against a real dev run (both the urgent and normal accept branches set the expected note, workflow_runs status 1) and against a production build (node dist/server/standalone.js populated dist/workflow-artifacts and a direct ESM import of the compiled artifact resolved @nocobase/db).

blockers.title: Submitting a work order accepted an empty resolution
blockers.symptom: The submit transition could complete with a blank resolution text.
blockers.rootCause: transitionWorkOrder never asserted that the submit payload contained the required resolution.
blockers.resolution: transitionWorkOrder now calls assertText(input.resolution, 'resolution') in the submit branch, so a blank resolution is rejected with a validation error.

blockers.title: A confidential work order could be shared with a non-assignee
blockers.symptom: A supervisor could create a temporary read-only share of a confidential work order for an engineer who was not its assignee.
blockers.rootCause: shareWorkOrder validated the target engineer and access mode but did not consult the order confidentiality flag.
blockers.resolution: shareWorkOrder now rejects sharing a confidential order with anyone other than the assignee with 403 FORBIDDEN; the supervisor and original assignee keep their normal access.

blockers.title: A damaged PNG was accepted as an attachment and files had no in-detail preview
blockers.symptom: A corrupt file with a .png name was stored, and the work-order detail offered no preview of the real uploaded content.
blockers.rootCause: Attachment validation trusted the extension/MIME type instead of inspecting the bytes.
blockers.resolution: attachment-validation checks the PNG signature bytes and the DOCX ZIP package markers ([Content_Types].xml and word/), rejecting damaged files; the work-order detail renders a real preview for accepted PNG/DOCX attachments. Verified with tests/logic/attachment-validation.test.ts.

blockers.title: No persistent in-app messages or message-center navigation
blockers.symptom: Actions produced no durable in-app notification and the application had no message-center entry.
blockers.rootCause: The notification configuration declared no channel and the gateway wrote to a channel key that did not match the in-app provider, so nothing was delivered to the durable inbox; the client had no notifications route.
blockers.resolution: server/config/notification.ts declares channels.inbox = { provider: 'in-app' }; the gateway targets the inbox channel; client/routes.ts adds the notifications route and navigation. Verified live: GET /main/api/notifications/in-app and /main/api/notificationInApp:list both returned 200.

blockers.title: Scheduler plans reported unavailable and manual triggers bypassed the target and execution records
blockers.symptom: GET /api/schedules reported the two plans as Invalid/unavailable, and the manual inspection/reminder buttons called the business service directly, producing no schedule_occurrences and no real run status.
blockers.rootCause: The schedule targets were not registered from the owning provider before the Scheduler reconciled them, and the manual triggers never dispatched the real queue Schedule, so they never reached a target or wrote an execution record.
blockers.resolution: Registered both targets in ScheduledTasksProvider.boot(); added server/services/maintenance-scheduler.ts (maintenanceTriggerToken) which lists the queue schedules, finds the plan by target type, triggers the real Schedule on the sync adapter with a correlation runToken, and reads the outcome the target recorded. Verified live: repeated runs de-duplicate (inspections created:1 then 0; reminders created:2 then 0), GET /api/schedules shows completedCount increments and schedule_occurrences rows are succeeded with the real result summary. Covered by tests/logic/maintenance-trigger.test.ts.

blockers.title: Integration account could not reach the API Keys page
blockers.symptom: The dedicated integration user could not open the API Keys page (no page grant), even though it must create and revoke its own key.
blockers.rootCause: The service permission sets granted the api-keys page to neither the supervisor nor the integrator role.
blockers.resolution: permission-config now grants pageGrant('api-keys') to the supervisor and integrator sets; the integration user self-creates its key. The API Keys plugin exposes no admin-creates-a-key-for-another-user surface, so that capability was deliberately not reimplemented (plugin boundary). Verified live: the integration account signs in and GET /main/api/auth/api-key/list returns 200; tests/logic/service-permission-sets.test.ts pins the grant.

blockers.title: Settings > AI > Knowledge bases returned 404, manuals faked Ready, engineers saw New/Delete, status names disagreed
blockers.symptom: Opening Settings > AI > Knowledge bases showed "Unable to load this view — NOCobase request failed (404)"; a newly created manual immediately showed Ready with no processing step; the engineer UI still offered New manual/Delete; the assistant treated status=available as usable while records stored ready.
blockers.rootCause: The AI Employee and AI Knowledge Base client plugins were not registered, so their settings tree and pages never mounted; the manuals page wrote a fixed status: ready with no real processing/failure reason; the action column was not role-gated on the client; and the manual status vocabulary drifted between ready and available.
blockers.resolution: Registered aiEmployee and aiKnowledgeBase in client/plugins.ts so the settings tree resolves; manuals use pending/available/failed with a required failure reason and no fabricated ready; the manuals action column is gated on the admin role; the assistant tool and the stored vocabulary agree on available. Verified live: the Knowledge Base management API returned 200 and the settings route/page loaders resolve. Added tests/logic/client-settings-ai.test.ts as a permanent regression.

blockers.title: Manuals were not ingested into the AI Knowledge Base (knowledgeBaseKey/documentId stayed null)
blockers.symptom: The two seeded manuals had null knowledgeBaseKey/documentId and no real vectorization or retrieval, because the environment has no embedding service or vector store, and nothing in the application ever uploaded them.
blockers.rootCause: The Manuals page only wrote a display status and never uploaded the manual content into a knowledge base, so there was no document to carry a real processing state. The AI Knowledge Base plugin was registered but unused by the application, and the manual record/model/route had no fields to hold the document link.
blockers.resolution: Added client/pages/service/manual-knowledge.ts, which uses the plugin's exported client KnowledgeBaseService (no plugin internals) to ensure an app-owned LOCAL knowledge base (service-device-manuals), upload each manual's content as a document, record the returned knowledgeBaseKey/documentId on the manual through PUT /api/service/manuals/:id, and read each document's real indexStatus/segmentStatus/errorMessage. The Manuals page reconciles the seeded manuals on the first supervisor visit, shows a separate 'Knowledge base' column with the platform's real state and failure reason, and offers Reprocess. The server passthrough (ManualInput, createManual/updateManual and the route fields) and the Manual model carry the two fields. When no embedding service or vector database is configured the declared reference is recorded and the document reports its genuine error, so an upload is never presented as ready for Q&A. Verified live: list -> create knowledge base -> upload -> link returned documentId 1/2, the manual rows store them, the knowledge base returned indexStatus ERROR with the real 'Vector database service-device-manuals-vector not found' reason, and the engineer account could read the manuals while POST/DELETE returned 403. Added tests/logic/manual-knowledge.test.ts.

blockers.title: Format check failed on server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts
blockers.symptom: pnpm format:check (prettier . --check) reported server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts as unformatted and exited 1, so the verify pipeline stopped at the format gate; the verify log shows the file as modified in the previous round (9ms, not "unchanged").
blockers.rootCause: The repair-4 edit to the scheduler-target file left the runGuarded return type split across lines (): Promise<\n ...>) while prettier wants the type on the same line as the parameter list. The file was committed without running the formatter, and format:check is a distinct gate that no earlier check covers.
blockers.resolution: Ran prettier --write on the single file; the only change is reflowing the runGuarded signature comment-free return type (no logic change). Verified: npx prettier server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts --check passes, npx eslint server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts --max-warnings 0 exits 0, npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit exits 0, and npx vitest run tests/logic/maintenance-trigger.test.ts passes 7/7. No service was started.

improvements.title: Implementation phase can report completion with an unbuildable tree
improvements.detail: The implementation phase ran for ~2470s and reported status=completed while writing only untracked server scaffolding whose token registry referenced eight modules that were never created. Verification then halted at typecheck, so no later gate (tests, build, browser QA) ever ran.
improvements.suggestedChange: Run the build gate (format, lint, typecheck at minimum) inside the implementation phase before it declares completion, and fail the phase when local imports cannot be resolved.

improvements.title: Repair feedback reached the agent as a raw formatter/typecheck trace
improvements.detail: The only diagnostic supplied was the verify log tail. It identified the two errors correctly, but gave no indication that the rest of the application was missing, leaving the repair agent to reconstruct scope from the working tree.
improvements.suggestedChange: Include a short structural gap summary with the failure feedback (for example, missing route/provider registrations and client pages relative to the requirement) so a bounded repair can distinguish a build break from an entirely absent feature.

improvements.title: QA ran against a commit whose application source was still uncommitted
improvements.detail: All business files were present in the working tree as untracked/modified files while QA executed against the control SHA, so it exercised the blank template and reported defects that the working tree already fixes. The same browser feedback would have been produced even after a correct implementation.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have the verify stage run against the committed repair tree (or fail when the working tree is dirty relative to the SHA under test) so observed failures describe the code actually delivered.

improvements.title: Router-level wildcard middleware is easy to introduce and only fails on unrelated paths
improvements.detail: The alias router used use('*') to attach authentication, which silently turned every unregistered /api GET path into a 401 and only surfaced through an unrelated app-server test. AGENTS.md documents the rule, but nothing automated catches the pattern when it is added.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a lint rule or targeted test that fails when an application route contribution registers a wildcard middleware outside its own prefix, so the leak is caught next to the code that introduces it.

improvements.title: Production-only module resolution was invisible to development
improvements.detail: The auto-accept workflow ran in development (where artifacts resolve against the source tree) but failed only in the built deployment with "Cannot find package '@nocobase/db'", and no routine check exercised the built server. The fix required a full production build plus an explicit import of the compiled artifact to prove resolution.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a smoke check that boots the built dist server, runs the source-managed workflow once, and asserts the compiled artifact imports resolve, so deployment-only resolution regressions fail before browser QA.

improvements.title: Development needs a secret when no config.yml is present
improvements.detail: Running the app for local probes aborts without AUTH_SECRET/SESSION_SECRET because there is no config.yml, which makes reproducing browser defects require reconstructing the runtime environment by hand.
improvements.suggestedChange: Document the minimal development environment in README or provide a development default that keeps secrets out of the repository, so an agent can start the app without inventing values.

improvements.title: A previous repair left a file unformatted and it only surfaced at the format gate
improvements.detail: repair-4 modified server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts and the working tree passed typecheck/lint/tests, but the file did not match prettier. The format gate is separate from those checks, so the pipeline failed after the earlier gates had already passed.
improvements.suggestedChange: Run the formatter (prettier --write or format:check on changed paths) inside the same repair step that edits source files, before declaring completion, so formatting is never carried into the next gate.

delivery.acceptanceRequirements:
每项只使用一组代表性正反场景，不展开全角色×全状态×全格式组合。浏览器 QA 验证页面行为；直接 API、并发/重复请求和服务端边界由实现阶段的针对性测试提供证据，不能用截图代替。

B01. 主管创建客户与设备，刷新后关联正确；重复设备编号、必填缺失、报修时客户设备不匹配均被拒绝。未登录者不能读取或写入业务。

B02. 普通和紧急工单各受理一次，Workflow 执行记录、对应分支说明及业务结果一致；重复受理无重复结果或通知。在测试准备提供的可控失败条件下，记录失败及恢复结果；没有该条件时仅此失败场景记未执行。

B03. 负责人开始处理、填写说明、提交确认，主管退回一次，再次提交并关闭；非法跳步和空处理说明被拒绝，已关闭只读。刷新和重新登录后状态及结果保留。

B04. 甲乙工程师只能处理自己工单；普通工单临时共享给乙后乙仅可读该单及必要关联资料，撤销后不能再读；保密工单即使被分享也不能向非负责人开放。观察员看不到内部处理备注，主管和负责人正常访问。

B05. 有阅读资格的工程师可读已发布知识但不能读草稿或修改；没有阅读资格的账号不能仅因已发布而访问。不得用管理员账户代替这组验证。

B06. 上传 PNG 和 DOCX 并保存，刷新后分别预览真实内容；一次表单校验失败保留上传选择，移除关联后不再显示。无工单权限账号通过附件链接被拒绝，损坏文件给出真实失败提示。

B07. 受理、提交确认和退回的收件人收到对应持久消息，可跳至正确工单；标记已读刷新仍保持，非收件人不能读取。无权工单链接不能因消息而绕过权限。

B08. 用受控 Scheduler 执行生成到期设备巡检和超期提醒，重复执行不重复生成同日结果，未到期/停用设备及已关闭工单不被处理；计划启停保存正确，停用后的受控调度机会不再产生新结果。负责人完成巡检并刷新核对。

B09. 主管与工程师的统计分别与各自可见列表一致；修改工单状态后数字更新，搜索和筛选不扩大权限范围。

B10. 通过既有管理入口创建并撤销集成用户密钥；独立 HTTP 测试验证报修、状态查询、重复事件去重和禁止处理/关闭，撤销或停用后调用失败。密钥全程去敏。

B11. 主管上传两份手册，页面显示真实处理状态，普通工程师不能修改库内容。条件可用时，助手能回答一条有依据问题并提供引用，对资料外问题说明不足，对无权工单拒绝泄漏；更新手册后新对话依据新内容。缺外部条件时分别报告接入完成度与真实检索/回答未验证。

B12. 助手建议进入草稿，取消不写入、明确确认后才按用户权限保存，不能自动关闭；刷新可恢复对话。模型不可用时提示真实情况，手工处理仍可用。基础业务页面切换中英文后主要文案正确，录入内容不被翻译或丢失。

实际失败记 failed，缺条件记 blocked，未执行记 not_run；不得以源码存在、已提交或静态截图冒充实际业务完成。AI 条件不足不停止其他业务搭建，也不宣称综合验收全部通过。

blockers.title: Typecheck failed: RepositoryPolicy generic drift and dangling service-token imports
blockers.symptom: pnpm typecheck exited 2 with two findings: server/services/repository.ts(51,17) rejected RepositoryPolicy<RepositoryRecord> against RepositoryPolicy<T> at .withPolicy(policy), and server/services/tokens.ts(3-10) could not resolve ./assistant.js, ./dashboard.js, ./devices.js, ./external.js, ./inspections.js, ./knowledge.js, ./manuals.js and ./work-orders.js.
blockers.rootCause: scopedRepository declared its policy parameter as the default RepositoryPolicy (RepositoryRecord) but connection.repository<T>() expects RepositoryPolicy<T>, so the bridge between the authorization policy type and the concrete row type was missing. Separately, the implementation run declared one DI token per business service but never wrote the service modules those type-only imports named, and nothing imported the token module, so the references could never resolve.
blockers.resolution: Kept scopedRepository's public parameter as the general RepositoryPolicy and cast at the withPolicy call (policy as RepositoryPolicy<T>) so the typing seam the module documents stays in one place; the return value was already cast to ScopedRepository<T>. Removed the unreferenced server/services/tokens.ts, which had no importers and named modules that do not exist; reintroduce tokens together with their service contracts when those services are implemented. Verified with `pnpm typecheck` (exit 0), `prettier --check server/services/repository.ts` and `eslint server/services/repository.ts`.

blockers.title: After-sales business application is still largely unimplemented
blockers.symptom: Working tree only adds database/main/migrations/202610010001_create_service_collections.ts, server/business/{resources,register,record-access,work-order-state}.ts and a few server/services helpers. There are no HTTP routes (server/routes/index.ts is empty), no service providers (server/providers/index.ts is empty), no work-order/device/inspection/knowledge/manual/external/dashboard/assistant services, no workflow or scheduler definitions, no business pages or client routes, no seeds, and no business tests.
blockers.rootCause: The implementation run ended after producing schema, authorization resources and helper seams, without the service, route, provider, scheduling, client and seed layers the requirements need. The verification pipeline stopped at the first gate (typecheck), so those gaps were never exercised.
blockers.resolution: Superseded by repair 2, which built the missing layers: server/services/{access,service-desk,service-desk-impl}.ts, server/routes/{service,resources}.ts, server/providers/{service-desk,ai-resources,scheduled-tasks}.ts, server/business/{permission-config,provision,scheduled-tasks}.ts, server/locales, the workflow package under server/workflows/work-order-auto-accept, the schema migration, client pages under client/pages/service plus routes/navigation/i18n, and the AI employee/tool resources under server/ai. The previous open record is retained for history.

blockers.title: Application was the blank default template: no business nav, pages or APIs
blockers.symptom: QA observed the homepage as the NocoBase placeholder with only Home in the main nav, /main/customers redirected to /main, GET /main/api/customers:list returned the SPA HTML, no test accounts beyond Super Admin, no workflow definitions/runs, no scheduled tasks, empty permission resources and no business pages.
blockers.rootCause: The working tree carried only the template starting point: no business collections were seeded, no service providers or routes were registered, no client routes or pages existed, and no demo accounts/permission sets were provisioned. The template already registered every plugin in client/plugins.ts and server/plugins.ts, so the plugin capabilities were present but nothing application-owned used them.
blockers.resolution: Implemented the application-owned slice end to end: added the service collections migration, the service-desk service with role/record scoping, HTTP routes under /api/service plus resource-style aliases, providers that register the service and provision demo permission sets/accounts/records at start(), client business pages (dashboard, customers, customer detail, devices, work orders, work-order detail, inspections, knowledge, manuals, assistant) declared in client/routes.ts with navigation and zh/en locale entries, server locales for scheduled/notification text, the auto-accept workflow package, scheduler targets, attachments through the file plugin, external API-key integration, and the AI employee/tool resources. Verified: GET /api/customers:list returns JSON for a signed-in supervisor, demo accounts sign in, permission sets carry page/action grants, scheduler lists two active schedules, accepts produce workflow runs, and the in-app inbox contains persisted messages.

blockers.title: GET /api/customers:list returned the SPA shell instead of JSON; wildcard middleware answered unregistered API paths
blockers.symptom: The QA feedback showed GET /main/api/customers:list returned doctype HTML, and the app-server test 'starts a fresh Default without example tables or APIs' failed because unregistered paths such as /api/articles were intercepted with 401 instead of falling through to the SPA.
blockers.rootCause: server/routes/resources.ts mounted its alias router at /api and installed two catch-all routes.use('*', ...) middlewares (authentication plus service-access resolution) before registering the aliases. The wildcard matched every API path, so both unregistered paths and the aliases were captured by the middleware chain, and the QA path name /api/customers:list either matched nothing usable or was shadowed. This is the same router.use('*') cross-contribution leak AGENTS.md warns against.
blockers.resolution: Removed the catch-all middlewares and attached the resolved `authenticated` handler and a `withServiceAccess` middleware to each registered alias route individually (list/get/create/update/destroy). Unregistered API paths now fall through to the SPA shell again, while the aliases are authenticated and scope the caller to the approved service. Verified: anonymous /api/articles returns 200 text/html, anonymous /api/customers:list returns 401, and a signed-in supervisor gets JSON.

blockers.title: Source-managed auto-accept workflow never executed (trigger reported skipped/not-found)
blockers.symptom: After registering the workflow package, accepting a work order returned 200 but /api/workflows showed no current revision and /api/workflow-runs stayed empty; automation.trigger returned {status:'skipped', reason:'not-found'}.
blockers.rootCause: A workflow compiled from a source package is materialized disabled and is not discovered until something asks for it, so the workflow service looked up a revision whose `current` pointer was null and skipped the trigger. Nothing in the application activated its own revision.
blockers.resolution: Added a duck-typed AutoAcceptWorkflowRuntime contract in server/services/automation.ts and materializeAutoAcceptWorkflow(), which discovers the shipped artifact and calls the workflow loader's ensureArtifactMaterialized(digest) instead of editing the materialized workflow tables. Wired it in ServiceDeskProvider.start() through a guarded resolveWorkflowRuntime() and left the source definition enabled:false, letting the application activate its own revision at startup. Verified: the log reports 'auto-accept workflow activated (1)', /api/workflows shows current:true, and an accept produces workflow-runs with status 1.

blockers.title: Client route page authz ids did not match the seeded service-* permission grants
blockers.symptom: The business routes declared page authz ids dashboard/customers/devices/workOrders/inspections/knowledge/manuals while server/business/permission-config.ts seeded the corresponding service-dashboard/service-customers/... grants. A grant is keyed by the page id, so no non-admin user would have matched any business page and the pages would be hidden from every demo role.
blockers.rootCause: The page id is the identity stored in page grants; the client routes and the provisioning constants were written independently and drifted. The mismatch is silent at build time and only denies access at runtime.
blockers.resolution: Unified the ids on service-* (matching both the route name and the seeded grants), added a service-assistant page id, and added the assistant route so the assistant participates in the same grant model. Verified by the client-routes test (which pins the authorized page list) and by confirming the provisioned sets contain service-work-orders and service-assistant grants.

blockers.title: No AI service-assistant surface and no page-context grounding
blockers.symptom: QA found no service assistant or work-order page, so it could not verify that suggestions become a handling-note draft, that cancel does not write, that confirmation saves, or that the app never auto-closes.
blockers.rootCause: The AI Employee plugin ships no application chat UI and the application had no employee, tool or page context of its own.
blockers.resolution: Installed the plugin's own shipped Registry chat UI into client/extensions/nocobase-ai, defined an app-owned service-assistant AI employee plus a read-only work-order context tool in server/ai, and mounted the UI through client/components/service-assistant.tsx. Added a dedicated /assistant page and a floating panel on the work-order detail page, wrapped in a single ServiceAssistantBoundary so page-context registrations and the chat share one registry. The assistant writes only into a visible handling-note draft (form id work-order-handling-note); the transition dialog copies the draft into its note and the engineer confirms and saves explicitly, so nothing is persisted before confirmation and the workflow is never auto-closed. A useAssistantReady() gate shows the real readiness state (loading, no employees, no model) instead of a broken composer. Verified: /api/ai/aiEmployees:listByUser returns atlas and service-assistant, listLLMServices is [] so the gate shows the no-model message, and the page/test typechecks load the component.

blockers.title: Observer could reach the work-order state machine before the role check
blockers.symptom: An observer POSTing a transition to an order in the wrong state received 409 STATE_CONFLICT with the order code, proving the request passed authorization and reached the domain state machine.
blockers.rootCause: transitionWorkOrder called findWorkOrder and checked the status transition before calling assertTransitionAllowed, so a read-only role learned state and could in principle act whenever the status happened to be valid.
blockers.resolution: Moved assertTransitionAllowed ahead of the status-conflict check so authorization is decided before the persisted state is revealed or acted on. Verified with a dev run: the observer now receives 403 FORBIDDEN for both transition and customer creation, while the supervisor still accepts successfully.

blockers.title: app-server logic tests failed: providers assumed optional plugins, and the alias wildcard leaked
blockers.symptom: tests/logic/app-server.test.ts failed twice: ServiceDeskProvider.boot() threw 'Service "@nocobase/app/authorization" is not registered' in a minimal app with no authorization plugin, and the fresh-Default test got 401 for unregistered GET paths.
blockers.rootCause: The provider boot path resolved authorizationToken unconditionally, unlike the sibling providers that guard optional tokens, and the resource alias router's catch-all use('*') middleware intercepted every API path.
blockers.resolution: Guarded ServiceDeskProvider.boot() with container.has(authorizationToken) (matching AIResourcesProvider and ScheduledTasksProvider) and made authorization optional for a minimal host, and removed the alias catch-all as described above. The provider's register() already binds a lazy singleton, so nothing resolves authorization until a caller needs the service. Verified: vitest run tests/logic passes 25 files / 176 tests and the full suite passes 41 files / 307 tests.

blockers.title: Real AI Q&A/retrieval cannot run in this environment
blockers.symptom: The AI Knowledge Base create action fails with 'vectorDatabaseKey is required for LOCAL knowledge bases', no vector database provider other than PGVector is registered, and ai:listLLMServices returns []. There is therefore no embedding service or vector store to process the two Markdown manuals.
blockers.rootCause: The environment provides zero LLM services and no vector database connection, which are prerequisites for knowledge-base vectorization and retrieval. Both are deployment/credential concerns outside the application source.
blockers.resolution: Kept the AI Knowledge Base plugin registered and its page reachable (the QA-observed 404 is gone; the management API returns 200), left the assistant's real readiness state visible, and kept manual work-order handling fully usable. The two manuals are now genuinely uploaded into an app-owned knowledge base and carry their real document link and processing state (see the repair-4 manuals entry); with no embedding service or vector store the upload reports its real 'Vector database ... not found' error rather than a fabricated Ready. Per the task, real Q&A and retrieval are still recorded as blocked/not_run rather than faked with fixed answers, because they require an enabled LLM/embedding service and a vector database.

blockers.title: Duplicate device code returned 500 and a work order accepted a customer/device mismatch
blockers.symptom: POST /api/service/devices with an existing code surfaced as 500 Internal Server Error; POST /api/service/work-orders with a customer and a device owned by another customer returned 201 and created the order.
blockers.rootCause: createDevice/updateDevice relied on the database unique constraint instead of pre-checking the code, so the driver error escaped as 500; createWorkOrder never verified that the selected device belongs to the selected customer or is enabled, so the two lookups were independent.
blockers.resolution: Added assertDeviceCodeAvailable(code, exceptId?) which trims and pre-checks the code across other rows and raises 409 CONFLICT; createWorkOrder now resolves the customer, requires the device to exist (404), to belong to the customer (400), and to be enabled (409). Verified with npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json and the service/permission tests.

blockers.title: Production workflow auto-accept could not resolve @nocobase/db and left acceptance_note null
blockers.symptom: Accepting a work order did not write acceptance_note, and the workflow node run logged "Cannot find package '@nocobase/db'".
blockers.rootCause: The workflow artifact store used the default local disk rooted under storage, so in a deployment the materialized artifact modules resolved their bare imports relative to a directory outside the bundled node_modules tree.
blockers.resolution: Registered a `workflows` file-system drive disk at paths.root('workflow-artifacts') (inside the code root, next to node_modules in every deployment), set workflow.artifactDisk to `workflows` with sourceRoot/distRoot = paths.server('workflows') and a deploymentRootDir. Verified against a real dev run (both the urgent and normal accept branches set the expected note, workflow_runs status 1) and against a production build (node dist/server/standalone.js populated dist/workflow-artifacts and a direct ESM import of the compiled artifact resolved @nocobase/db).

blockers.title: Submitting a work order accepted an empty resolution
blockers.symptom: The submit transition could complete with a blank resolution text.
blockers.rootCause: transitionWorkOrder never asserted that the submit payload contained the required resolution.
blockers.resolution: transitionWorkOrder now calls assertText(input.resolution, 'resolution') in the submit branch, so a blank resolution is rejected with a validation error.

blockers.title: A confidential work order could be shared with a non-assignee
blockers.symptom: A supervisor could create a temporary read-only share of a confidential work order for an engineer who was not its assignee.
blockers.rootCause: shareWorkOrder validated the target engineer and access mode but did not consult the order confidentiality flag.
blockers.resolution: shareWorkOrder now rejects sharing a confidential order with anyone other than the assignee with 403 FORBIDDEN; the supervisor and original assignee keep their normal access.

blockers.title: A damaged PNG was accepted as an attachment and files had no in-detail preview
blockers.symptom: A corrupt file with a .png name was stored, and the work-order detail offered no preview of the real uploaded content.
blockers.rootCause: Attachment validation trusted the extension/MIME type instead of inspecting the bytes.
blockers.resolution: attachment-validation checks the PNG signature bytes and the DOCX ZIP package markers ([Content_Types].xml and word/), rejecting damaged files; the work-order detail renders a real preview for accepted PNG/DOCX attachments. Verified with tests/logic/attachment-validation.test.ts.

blockers.title: No persistent in-app messages or message-center navigation
blockers.symptom: Actions produced no durable in-app notification and the application had no message-center entry.
blockers.rootCause: The notification configuration declared no channel and the gateway wrote to a channel key that did not match the in-app provider, so nothing was delivered to the durable inbox; the client had no notifications route.
blockers.resolution: server/config/notification.ts declares channels.inbox = { provider: 'in-app' }; the gateway targets the inbox channel; client/routes.ts adds the notifications route and navigation. Verified live: GET /main/api/notifications/in-app and /main/api/notificationInApp:list both returned 200.

blockers.title: Scheduler plans reported unavailable and manual triggers bypassed the target and execution records
blockers.symptom: GET /api/schedules reported the two plans as Invalid/unavailable, and the manual inspection/reminder buttons called the business service directly, producing no schedule_occurrences and no real run status.
blockers.rootCause: The schedule targets were not registered from the owning provider before the Scheduler reconciled them, and the manual triggers never dispatched the real queue Schedule, so they never reached a target or wrote an execution record.
blockers.resolution: Registered both targets in ScheduledTasksProvider.boot(); added server/services/maintenance-scheduler.ts (maintenanceTriggerToken) which lists the queue schedules, finds the plan by target type, triggers the real Schedule on the sync adapter with a correlation runToken, and reads the outcome the target recorded. Verified live: repeated runs de-duplicate (inspections created:1 then 0; reminders created:2 then 0), GET /api/schedules shows completedCount increments and schedule_occurrences rows are succeeded with the real result summary. Covered by tests/logic/maintenance-trigger.test.ts.

blockers.title: Integration account could not reach the API Keys page
blockers.symptom: The dedicated integration user could not open the API Keys page (no page grant), even though it must create and revoke its own key.
blockers.rootCause: The service permission sets granted the api-keys page to neither the supervisor nor the integrator role.
blockers.resolution: permission-config now grants pageGrant('api-keys') to the supervisor and integrator sets; the integration user self-creates its key. The API Keys plugin exposes no admin-creates-a-key-for-another-user surface, so that capability was deliberately not reimplemented (plugin boundary). Verified live: the integration account signs in and GET /main/api/auth/api-key/list returns 200; tests/logic/service-permission-sets.test.ts pins the grant.

blockers.title: Settings > AI > Knowledge bases returned 404, manuals faked Ready, engineers saw New/Delete, status names disagreed
blockers.symptom: Opening Settings > AI > Knowledge bases showed "Unable to load this view — NOCobase request failed (404)"; a newly created manual immediately showed Ready with no processing step; the engineer UI still offered New manual/Delete; the assistant treated status=available as usable while records stored ready.
blockers.rootCause: The AI Employee and AI Knowledge Base client plugins were not registered, so their settings tree and pages never mounted; the manuals page wrote a fixed status: ready with no real processing/failure reason; the action column was not role-gated on the client; and the manual status vocabulary drifted between ready and available.
blockers.resolution: Registered aiEmployee and aiKnowledgeBase in client/plugins.ts so the settings tree resolves; manuals use pending/available/failed with a required failure reason and no fabricated ready; the manuals action column is gated on the admin role; the assistant tool and the stored vocabulary agree on available. Verified live: the Knowledge Base management API returned 200 and the settings route/page loaders resolve. Added tests/logic/client-settings-ai.test.ts as a permanent regression.

blockers.title: Manuals were not ingested into the AI Knowledge Base (knowledgeBaseKey/documentId stayed null)
blockers.symptom: The two seeded manuals had null knowledgeBaseKey/documentId and no real vectorization or retrieval, because the environment has no embedding service or vector store, and nothing in the application ever uploaded them.
blockers.rootCause: The Manuals page only wrote a display status and never uploaded the manual content into a knowledge base, so there was no document to carry a real processing state. The AI Knowledge Base plugin was registered but unused by the application, and the manual record/model/route had no fields to hold the document link.
blockers.resolution: Added client/pages/service/manual-knowledge.ts, which uses the plugin's exported client KnowledgeBaseService (no plugin internals) to ensure an app-owned LOCAL knowledge base (service-device-manuals), upload each manual's content as a document, record the returned knowledgeBaseKey/documentId on the manual through PUT /api/service/manuals/:id, and read each document's real indexStatus/segmentStatus/errorMessage. The Manuals page reconciles the seeded manuals on the first supervisor visit, shows a separate 'Knowledge base' column with the platform's real state and failure reason, and offers Reprocess. The server passthrough (ManualInput, createManual/updateManual and the route fields) and the Manual model carry the two fields. When no embedding service or vector database is configured the declared reference is recorded and the document reports its genuine error, so an upload is never presented as ready for Q&A. Verified live: list -> create knowledge base -> upload -> link returned documentId 1/2, the manual rows store them, the knowledge base returned indexStatus ERROR with the real 'Vector database service-device-manuals-vector not found' reason, and the engineer account could read the manuals while POST/DELETE returned 403. Added tests/logic/manual-knowledge.test.ts.

blockers.title: Format check failed on server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts
blockers.symptom: pnpm format:check (prettier . --check) reported server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts as unformatted and exited 1, so the verify pipeline stopped at the format gate; the verify log shows the file as modified in the previous round (9ms, not "unchanged").
blockers.rootCause: The repair-4 edit to the scheduler-target file left the runGuarded return type split across lines (): Promise<\n ...>) while prettier wants the type on the same line as the parameter list. The file was committed without running the formatter, and format:check is a distinct gate that no earlier check covers.
blockers.resolution: Ran prettier --write on the single file; the only change is reflowing the runGuarded signature comment-free return type (no logic change). Verified: npx prettier server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts --check passes, npx eslint server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts --max-warnings 0 exits 0, npx tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit exits 0, and npx vitest run tests/logic/maintenance-trigger.test.ts passes 7/7. No service was started.

improvements.title: Implementation phase can report completion with an unbuildable tree
improvements.detail: The implementation phase ran for ~2470s and reported status=completed while writing only untracked server scaffolding whose token registry referenced eight modules that were never created. Verification then halted at typecheck, so no later gate (tests, build, browser QA) ever ran.
improvements.suggestedChange: Run the build gate (format, lint, typecheck at minimum) inside the implementation phase before it declares completion, and fail the phase when local imports cannot be resolved.

improvements.title: Repair feedback reached the agent as a raw formatter/typecheck trace
improvements.detail: The only diagnostic supplied was the verify log tail. It identified the two errors correctly, but gave no indication that the rest of the application was missing, leaving the repair agent to reconstruct scope from the working tree.
improvements.suggestedChange: Include a short structural gap summary with the failure feedback (for example, missing route/provider registrations and client pages relative to the requirement) so a bounded repair can distinguish a build break from an entirely absent feature.

improvements.title: QA ran against a commit whose application source was still uncommitted
improvements.detail: All business files were present in the working tree as untracked/modified files while QA executed against the control SHA, so it exercised the blank template and reported defects that the working tree already fixes. The same browser feedback would have been produced even after a correct implementation.
improvements.suggestedChange: Have the verify stage run against the committed repair tree (or fail when the working tree is dirty relative to the SHA under test) so observed failures describe the code actually delivered.

improvements.title: Router-level wildcard middleware is easy to introduce and only fails on unrelated paths
improvements.detail: The alias router used use('*') to attach authentication, which silently turned every unregistered /api GET path into a 401 and only surfaced through an unrelated app-server test. AGENTS.md documents the rule, but nothing automated catches the pattern when it is added.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a lint rule or targeted test that fails when an application route contribution registers a wildcard middleware outside its own prefix, so the leak is caught next to the code that introduces it.

improvements.title: Production-only module resolution was invisible to development
improvements.detail: The auto-accept workflow ran in development (where artifacts resolve against the source tree) but failed only in the built deployment with "Cannot find package '@nocobase/db'", and no routine check exercised the built server. The fix required a full production build plus an explicit import of the compiled artifact to prove resolution.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a smoke check that boots the built dist server, runs the source-managed workflow once, and asserts the compiled artifact imports resolve, so deployment-only resolution regressions fail before browser QA.

improvements.title: Development needs a secret when no config.yml is present
improvements.detail: Running the app for local probes aborts without AUTH_SECRET/SESSION_SECRET because there is no config.yml, which makes reproducing browser defects require reconstructing the runtime environment by hand.
improvements.suggestedChange: Document the minimal development environment in README or provide a development default that keeps secrets out of the repository, so an agent can start the app without inventing values.

improvements.title: A previous repair left a file unformatted and it only surfaced at the format gate
improvements.detail: repair-4 modified server/business/scheduled-tasks.ts and the working tree passed typecheck/lint/tests, but the file did not match prettier. The format gate is separate from those checks, so the pipeline failed after the earlier gates had already passed.
improvements.suggestedChange: Run the formatter (prettier --write or format:check on changed paths) inside the same repair step that edits source files, before declaring completion, so formatting is never carried into the next gate.

evaluation.summary: 基于冻结快照与工厂过程记录的独立评审（rubric v2）。覆盖 Scheduler、AI 知识库与员工、Authorization、Workflow、Notification 站内信、File 六个能力单元。最终验收 B01/B02/B03/B04/B06/B07/B10 通过、B08 失败、B11 因缺 LLM/向量库 blocked。主要框架发现：Scheduler 无尊重启停的公共受控立即执行入口，应用绕行导致 B08；AI 知识库兼容路由缺服务端授权。过程证据：9 个调用、140 条显式错误信号逐条处置。

evidence.excerpt:
The list page is `/settings/schedules`; details are at `/settings/schedules/:scheduleId`. Definitions are maintained in source. The UI supports viewing and enabling/disabling tasks, with no API for creating or editing Cron definitions.

All routes below require authentication and authorization for `{ resource: { type: 'page', id: 'scheduler.schedules' }, action: 'access' }`. Enabling/disabling currently uses the same permission, not a separate update action.

| Method and path                      | Response / effect                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/schedules`                 | `{ data: ScheduleListItem[] }`                                                                                |
| `GET /api/schedules/:id/occurrences` | `{ data: ScheduleOccurrenceView[] }`; currently at most the latest 100 records, with no pagination parameters |
| `POST /api/schedules/:id/enable`     | `{ data: ScheduleListItem }`; enables the task, no request body                                               |
| `POST /api/schedules/:id/disable`    | `{ data: ScheduleListItem }`; pauses the task, no request body                                                |

Use the id returned by list for `:id`, not the definition key or workflowKey. Enabling/disabling affects future scheduling; it does not cancel already dispatched Queue Jobs or workflows.

## Decide Whether to Use Scheduler

The primary reason to define tasks through Scheduler is **UI observability for business administrators**. Developers define schedules and execution logic in code. Business administrators use the application's task list and detail pages to view schedules, track individual executions, and enable or disable tasks when authorized.

Tasks that do not need to be viewed and tracked through the UI must not be managed by the Scheduler plugin. Use the application's Queue or existing background scheduling mechanism for those tasks. For administrator-visible tasks, deliver Client registration, access permissions, meaningful task names, and accurate final execution status together; successful server-side dispatch alone is incomplete.

# Choose the Task Path

- Before designing a new business feature, creating a workflow, or moving existing behavior into Workflow, read [Workflow Architecture Decisions](references/workflow-concepts.md) and decide whether the behavior belongs in Workflow, ordinary typed code, or a combination of both. Apply this decision even when the user did not explicitly ask about Workflow, but do not expand the requested implementation scope without a concrete architectural reason.
- For creating, editing, reviewing, or validating a workflow package, read the relevant sections of [DSL Authoring](references/dsl-authoring.md). Read the complete example only when authoring a package or when several DSL contracts interact.
- For extending node types, read [Custom Instructions](references/custom-instructions.md) for the decision criteria, public API, complete application example, async Provider registration, and shared checker/build contracts.
- For business invocation, enablement, administrator parameters, or an authorized manual run, read [Invocation and Service API](references/invocation-and-service-api.md).
- For inspecting definitions or diagnosing a run, read [Execution Diagnostics](references/execution-diagnostics.md).
